rajesh: Quick sync after the RFC. Two competing models for routing + scope: (A) prefix/hint based routing + post-validate authn, (B) crypto-binder inside key so router can trust scope without DB. Thoughts?
sylvie: Prefers A. Hints keep issuance simple and let us evolve mappings without reissuing keys. But router MUST not make final allow/deny decisions on hint alone.
marco: B lowers latency but operationally heavy. Global signer rotation = high blast radius. Also stale roles become a problem; you can't change roles for a key without reissuing.
ops-lee: From ops: hybrid seems pragmatic. Allow hint for routing with strict validation downstream. Add metrics to detect hint->canonical mismatches. Also need backfill for legacy keys.
rajesh: Agreed. Proposed runtime behavior: router may use hint for pool selection, then authn service returns canonical principal + projects + roles. Audit must log the canonical project.
sylvie: Cache strategy: credential_id -> principal_snapshot (small TTL) + changefeed invalidation. Router caches only routing_hint derived from snapshot id. On rotation bump snapshot id to force invalidation.
marco: Edge-case: multi-project service keys. Router picks primary project for routing, authz uses full project list. Must document and monitor.
ops-lee: Failure modes: if authn is degraded allow routers to use last-known snapshot for N seconds, then enter safe-mode (deny high-privilege verbs). Add an alert when fail-open occurs.
sec-bot: Audit requirement AR-12: every accepted request must log principal_id, project_id(s), credential_id, action, and decision.
rajesh: Action items: (1) compatibility proxy spec for legacy prefixes (rajesh), (2) cache/changefeed contract (sylvie), (3) fail-open/safe-mode runbook + metrics (ops-lee). We'll reconvene in eng-security next week. Thanks all :thumbsup:
